plan.title: AD lesional vs control DE + hallmark GSEA
plan.analytical_narrative:
The input is a single-batch bulk RNA-seq count matrix from Salmon (12,000 gene symbols x 12 samples) with an unpaired 6 lesional atopic dermatitis vs 6 control design, plus a 12x2 metadata table carrying only `condition`. The research question has two parts — which genes change, and which hallmark pathways change — and one explicit caveat: sample_01 has a library size roughly 4x below the median.

The plan therefore starts with a QC/depth step (T1S1) that quantifies the depth of sample_01 in context, checks whether it is also a clustering outlier after variance-stabilising transformation, and computes DESeq2 size factors and a Cook's-distance profile. The point is to decide about that sample on evidence rather than by rule of thumb: low depth alone is not grounds for exclusion, because DESeq2's negative-binomial model with median-of-ratios normalisation handles unequal depth by construction; a sample that is both shallow AND an outlier in PC space and on Cook's distance is another matter. T1S1 emits a documented keep/drop recommendation but does not itself decide the primary analysis.

T1S2 runs the differential expression as DESeq2 ~condition on all 12 samples — this is the primary result, because dropping a sample from an n=6 vs n=6 design costs real power and the standard model already accommodates depth differences. T1S2 then repeats the identical contrast with sample_01 removed as a pre-specified sensitivity analysis, and reports the concordance of the two result sets. If the shallow sample were driving the calls, that comparison is what exposes it; the pair of tables is more informative than either alone. Shrunken log2 fold changes (apeglm) are used for ranking and for the volcano, unshrunken Wald statistics for the GSEA ranking.

T1S3 takes the full ranked gene list — not a thresholded DE subset — and runs preranked GSEA against the 50 MSigDB human hallmark sets staged in this environment (human, HGNC symbols, matching the counts matrix's gene-symbol row index). Preranked GSEA rather than over-representation because with n=6 per group the number of FDR-significant genes may be small and a hard cutoff would throw away the ranking information. The same GSEA is run on the sensitivity ranking so the pathway conclusions carry the same robustness check as the gene-level ones.

With 12,000 genes x 12 samples the whole analysis is small — a few MB — so resources are modest throughout.

With n=6 per group, PCA separation by condition may be modest; do not over-read PC1.
Shallow samples show fewer detected genes and more apparent zeros; that is expected and is not independent evidence of an outlier.

steps.name: DESeq2 differential expression: lesional vs control, with sample_01 sensitivity
steps.question: Which genes are differentially expressed between atopic dermatitis lesional skin and control skin, and do those calls survive removal of the shallow sample_01?
steps.description: Run DESeq2 on the raw counts with design ~condition, control as the reference level so log2 fold changes read as lesional-vs-control. PRIMARY analysis uses all 12 samples. Pre-filter genes with a low-count filter (e.g. at least 10 counts in at least 6 samples — the size of the smaller group) before fitting; report how many of the 12,000 genes are retained. Report Wald test results with BH-adjusted p-values, and additionally compute apeglm-shrunken log2 fold changes for ranking and visualisation. Emit the full results table (gene symbol, baseMean, unshrunken and shrunken log2FC, lfcSE, Wald stat, pvalue, padj) sorted by padj, and report the count of genes at padj<0.05 with no fold-change cut and at padj<0.05 with |shrunken log2FC|>1, as separate numbers. SENSITIVITY analysis: re-run the identical pipeline on the 11 samples with sample_01 removed and compare — number of DE genes in each, overlap of the padj<0.05 sets, Spearman correlation of Wald statistics across commonly tested genes, and a scatter of shrunken log2FC (12-sample vs 11-sample) with top genes labelled. Produce an MA plot and a labelled volcano plot of the primary analysis. Also emit a ranking file for GSEA: gene symbol plus unshrunken Wald statistic, one for the primary fit and one for the sensitivity fit. If T1S1 recommended dropping sample_01, still report BOTH analyses and state plainly which is primary and why.
steps.context: 6 lesional vs 6 control, unpaired, single batch, no covariates beyond condition in the 12x2 metadata — the design is necessarily ~condition alone. Genes are HGNC-style symbols in the first column of counts.csv. T1S1 QC output (size factors, outlier verdict) is available as input.
constraints: Design is ~condition only; do not invent covariates the 12x2 metadata does not contain.
Set the reference level explicitly to the control group as named in metadata.csv — do not rely on alphabetical ordering without checking what it produces.
Treat the all-12-sample fit as primary and the 11-sample fit as a sensitivity analysis, unless T1S1 gave combined outlier evidence, in which case state the switch and its justification explicitly.
Use apeglm-shrunken LFCs for ranking and plotting, and the unshrunken Wald statistic for the GSEA ranking file.
Report how many genes pass the low-count filter out of the 12,000 input rows.
Do not report a fold-change-only gene list without its adjusted p-value.
Handle duplicated gene symbols in the first column explicitly (aggregate or de-duplicate) and report how many rows this affected.
acceptance_criteria: A full DESeq2 results table for all tested genes is written for the 12-sample primary fit, with padj and both shrunken and unshrunken log2FC.
A parallel results table exists for the 11-sample sensitivity fit with sample_01 removed.
Concordance between the two fits is quantified: DE-set overlap and Spearman correlation of Wald statistics.
Counts of significant genes are reported at padj<0.05 alone and at padj<0.05 with |log2FC|>1, as separate numbers.
MA plot and labelled volcano plot for the primary fit are saved.
Two GSEA ranking files (gene symbol + Wald statistic) are written, one per fit.
caveats: n=6 per group is modest; a small number of FDR-significant genes is a plausible and honest outcome, not a pipeline failure. Do not lower the FDR threshold to manufacture hits.
Shrunken LFCs must not be fed into the GSEA ranking as if they were test statistics — shrinkage compresses the tails and distorts the ranking.
If the two fits disagree substantially, that is a finding to report, not a problem to resolve by picking the nicer table.

steps.name: Hallmark preranked GSEA on the lesional-vs-control ranking
steps.question: Which of the 50 MSigDB hallmark pathways are coordinately up- or down-regulated in atopic dermatitis lesional skin versus control, and are those pathway calls stable when the shallow sample_01 is removed?
steps.description: Run preranked GSEA (fgsea, multilevel) on the whole-transcriptome ranking from T1S2 — gene symbol ranked by unshrunken DESeq2 Wald statistic — against the human hallmark gene set collection. The reference needed is the MSigDB hallmark collection for Homo sapiens as a symbols GMT; resolve it from the environment's reference store at run time rather than hard-coding a path, and confirm it is the human (HGNC symbol) file so it matches the gene-symbol row index of counts.csv. Report, for every hallmark set: set name, size after intersection with the tested background, normalised enrichment score, p-value, BH-adjusted p-value, and leading-edge genes. Rank by adjusted p-value and produce a dot/bar plot of significant sets (padj<0.05) coloured by NES direction, plus enrichment-curve plots for the top few sets in each direction. Repeat the identical GSEA on the sensitivity ranking (sample_01 removed) and report a side-by-side per-set NES comparison between the two rankings including their correlation, so the pathway conclusions carry the same robustness check as the gene-level ones. Separately, cross-reference how many T1S2 padj<0.05 genes fall in each significant set's leading edge, so pathway calls trace back to named genes.
steps.context: Skin, atopic dermatitis lesional vs control. The environment stages the MSigDB 2026.1 human hallmark collection (50 HALLMARK_* sets, HGNC symbols, GMT) alongside a mouse hallmark file and human GO/oncogenic collections — the human hallmark file is the one this step needs. Input rankings come from T1S2.
constraints: Use the human (Homo sapiens, HGNC symbol) hallmark collection, not the mouse one — the data is human skin.
Rank on the full tested gene list from T1S2, not on a padj-filtered subset; preranked GSEA needs the whole ranking.
Use the set of genes actually tested by DESeq2 as the universe; report per-set size after intersecting with that universe and drop sets left with fewer than 10 members, stating how many were dropped.
Report BH-adjusted p-values for all tested sets, not only the significant ones.
Set and report the random seed for the fgsea procedure so the result is reproducible.
Run the same analysis on the sample_01-removed ranking and report NES concordance between the two.
acceptance_criteria: A hallmark GSEA results table covering all tested sets is written, with NES, p, padj, set size, and leading-edge genes.
The gene set collection used is identified in the output by name and organism, and confirmed to be human.
Significant sets (padj<0.05) are plotted with NES direction shown; if none reach padj<0.05, that is reported explicitly along with the top sets by nominal p.
A parallel GSEA on the sample_01-removed ranking is reported with a per-set NES comparison against the primary ranking.
Leading-edge genes of significant sets are cross-referenced to the T1S2 significant gene list.
caveats: If the human hallmark collection cannot be resolved in the reference store at run time, stop and report that plainly — do not substitute the mouse hallmark file, a GO collection, or an internet download; the network is unavailable and a species-mismatched collection produces confident nonsense.

Hallmark sets overlap in membership (notably the inflammatory/interferon/TNF sets), so several co-significant sets can reflect one underlying signal — inspect leading edges for shared genes before reporting them as independent findings.
NES sign depends on the direction of the ranking; verify against a known-direction gene from T1S2 that positive NES means up in lesional skin.
GSEA on n=6 vs n=6 rests on gene-level statistics that are themselves noisy; report NES with adjusted p and avoid mechanistic claims from a single borderline set.
